contextAndProblemStatement: ADR-0001 chose managed PostgreSQL. Two years on, write volume has grown 40x and the managed tier's vertical limit is now the bottleneck; the schema has also drifted toward wide, document-shaped rows in the two hottest tables.
decisionDrivers: write throughput now exceeds the largest managed PostgreSQL tier
the two hottest tables are effectively documents already
the rest of the schema is still relational
consideredOptions: Move the two hot tables to DynamoDB, keep PostgreSQL for the rest

decisionOutcome.chosenOption: Move the two hot tables to DynamoDB, keep PostgreSQL for the rest
decisionOutcome.justification: it removes the bottleneck where it actually is without rewriting the relational core, and the team has since gained DynamoDB experience on another service.

positive: write throughput no longer bound by a single node
the relational schema and its tooling are untouched
negative: cross-store consistency must be handled in application code

confirmation: Load test at 2x current peak passes against the split datastore before cutover; ADR-0001 is marked superseded.
